topics.topic: What if humans never needed sleep?
topics.hookPromise: Explore what would happen to health, work, society, memory, and time if sleep suddenly became biologically unnecessary.

topics.topic: What if AI electricity demand grows faster than the grid can handle?
topics.hookPromise: Follow one hypothetical giant AI load from server rack to substation to regional grid, then show what really happens when compute scales faster than physical power infrastructure — delays, new supply, grid buildout, cost fights and flexible compute rather than an automatic blackout apocalypse.
evidenceSignals: Semrush US snapshot: 'AI data centers' about 12,100 monthly searches with a strongly rising recent trend.
Gartner 2026-06-10 forecasts worldwide data-center electricity consumption at 565 TWh in 2026, up 26% YoY, with AI-optimized servers at 31% of data-center electricity use.
IEA 2026 research says data-center investment and electricity use are surging while grid/supply-chain bottlenecks are becoming a central constraint.
EIA 2026 says data centers are a major driver of renewed U.S. electricity-demand growth after years of near-flat demand.
A current 2026 news cycle around power constraints, cost allocation and local opposition gives the topic immediate relevance without requiring a news-only script.

topics.topic: What if the next extreme solar storm is stronger than we planned for?
topics.hookPromise: Use NASA's July 2026 result as the fresh angle, then escalate through satellites, navigation, radio, power-grid stress and what modern infrastructure can actually survive without generic apocalypse claims.
evidenceSignals: NASA Goddard reported on 2026-07-15 that a NASA-led Nature paper suggests the assumed ceiling on Earth's response to solar storms may be an illusion.
Semrush US snapshot: solar flare about 40,500 monthly searches, solar storm about 27,100, Carrington event about 22,200.
NOAA documents direct impacts on power grids, GPS/GNSS, satellites, aviation and communications.

topics.topic: What if we tried to put out the Sun with water?
topics.hookPromise: Take the campfire intuition seriously, scale the water from oceans to planet-sized amounts, and reveal why adding water does not extinguish a star — it can add fuel and mass instead.
evidenceSignals: A June 2026 r/theydidthemath request asking how much water or ice would be needed to quench the Sun drew 142 points and 115 comments.
The core paradox is scientifically explainable with stellar structure, fusion, gravity, heating, and the composition of water rather than requiring unsupported speculation.
The premise has a simple visual ladder: bucket, ocean, water planet, stellar-scale mass, then the counterintuitive hotter/more massive outcome.
